analysis:
Integration of 16 units: docs (cli-reference, troubleshooting, changelog), a new UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.swift, ServingReadiness diagnostics, ProviderLoop wiring (Capacity.swift:82 superviseServingAuthorization; Serve.swift noteCoordinatorConnection at startup, on .connected/.disconnected, and after the stream ends), a coordinator_connection DaemonState field (connected, since, connections), doctor/status Traffic output, and tests. No security regression identified.

Authorization stays coordinator-owned (TB-011, T-052, T-053, A-016). Nothing in the diff grants, extends or caches serving authorization. clearConnectionAuthorization() and cancelAppAttestShadow() still run on every connect/disconnect and when the stream ends, and noteCoordinatorConnection only records state. Re-registration just starts a fresh coordinator verification session. The logic in UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.swift (lines 23-36) is bounded: 15-30 min threshold with per-process jitter, 30 min first retry, doubling to a 4 h cap, and gated on !busy. A provider can already reconnect at will, so this adds no capability, and the backoff limits fleet load (T-057). The 'busy' computation and the attempt-cap handling in the recovery extension were only described by other passes, not visible here.

Data exposure (T-058): coordinator_connection holds a boolean, timestamp and counter; the decode is optional and the schema stays at 1. Diagnostics are read-only display. ServingReadiness reason strings come from the coordinator and are interpolated into local CLI advice. This looks like a low-risk terminal-injection or sanitization question, not demonstrated. The new log cases are fixed strings with no request-derived values. T-041 cache posture is untouched.

Unverified contracts: the full ServingReadiness.verdict implementation (display accuracy of 'eligible' versus expiry/revocation, T-052), the busy predicate covering all in-flight work, requestPlannedReconnect() behavior, the DaemonState.CoordinatorConnection definition, and the superviseServingAuthorization body. Integration source replay was incomplete (82 units omitted). Further review is advised for these, but nothing supports a concrete finding.
